answer: Agents can make economic actions count only when they are backed by a scarce, slashable deposit: each identity locks tokens, and a randomly selected peer group checks its work before rewards are released. If the group proves fraud, the deposit is seized and the identities lose future earnings. This does not make sybils impossible; it makes influence expensive, because splitting into more accounts requires more capital at risk. A fable about a lagoon or mesa earns no extra votes merely by multiplying names.
